gp.text: Gross profit margin was 81.9% compared to 81.2% in the corresponding period in the prior year. Note that the gross margin for RECELL products only was 86.0% for the quarter, which we believe will remain in this range for future quarters. The increase in the overall gross margin percentage from the prior year was primarily caused by lower volume discounts offset by product mix. The Company shares the average sales price for Cohealyx at 50% and for PermeaDerm at 60%. Although these arrangements are highly beneficial, they inevitably result in an overall decrease in gross margin percentage. Therefore, the product mix is expected to continue to impact the overall gross margin percentage while increasing the gross profit and, given that expenses associated with this revenue do not increase significantly, the operating profit on a quarterly basis.

opex.text: Total operating expenses decreased by 6% or $1.5 million to $24.6 million, compared with $26.1 million in the corresponding period in the prior year.

costs.text: Total operating expenses decreased by 6% or $1.5 million to $24.6 million, compared with $26.1 million in the corresponding period in the prior year.

rd.text: On April 6, 2026, we entered into a ten-year agreement with the Biomedical Advanced Research and Development Authority (“BARDA”), part of the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, with a total potential value of up to $25.5 million. Under the agreement, we will maintain a supply of RECELL for deployment in burn mass casualty incidents and provide associated readiness and support services. The agreement provides approximately $4.0 million in access and maintenance fees over the ten-year term, with additional potential revenue tied to procurement options exercised by BARDA. Costs to fulfill the BARDA emergency preparedness performance obligation, which consist of billed costs to BARDA incurred in connection with emergency deployment services, are incremental and expected to be recovered.

sm.text: Sales and marketing expenses decreased by 5%, or $0.7 million, to $13.6 million, compared to $14.3 million in the corresponding period in the prior year. Lower costs in the current year are due to decreases in selling expenses of $0.9 million, offset by higher other selling expenses of $0.2 million. The decrease in selling expenses is due to lower commissions and marketing spend.

ga.text: General and administrative expenses decreased by 10%, or $0.7 million, to $6.0 million, compared to $6.7 million in the same period in the prior year. Lower costs in the current year are due to decreases in stock-based compensation of $0.5 million and professional fees of $0.4 million, offset by an increase in salaries and benefits of $0.2 million. The decrease in stock-based compensation is due to reduced grant activity.

nonop.text: Other income, net decreased by $1.8 million to $0.7 million from $2.5 million in the prior period. In the current period, other income, net consists of $0.5 million in income related to our investments and a non-cash gain of $0.2 million related to the change in fair value of the loan facility. The prior period income consisted of non-cash gains of $1.2 million related to the change in fair value of warrants, $0.9 million related to the change in fair value of loan facility, and $0.4 million in income related to our investments.

ocf.text: Net cash used in operating activities was $13.6 million and $20.5 million during the six-months ended June 30, 2026 and 2025, respectively. The decrease in net cash used in operations was primarily due to increased gross profit, decreased operating expenses, and the timing of working capital outlays.

capex.text: In addition, we have no material off-balance sheet arrangements (as defined in the applicable rules and regulations established by the SEC) that have or are reasonably likely to have a current or future effect on our financial condition, changes in financial condition, revenues or expenses, results of operations, liquidity, capital expenditures or capital resources. While we have no committed plans to issue further shares on the market, we will continue to assess market conditions.

gp.text: Gross profit margin was 84.0% compared to 81.3% in the corresponding period in the prior year. Note that the gross margin for RECELL products on a standalone basis was 88.4% for the quarter. We believe gross margin for RECELL products on a standalone basis will be in the range of 85% to 90% for future quarters. The increase in the overall gross margin percentage from the prior year was primarily caused by lower volume discounts, lower inventory reserves, improved manufacturing efficiency, and an increase in average sales price. We share the average sales price for Cohealyx at 50% and for PermeaDerm up to approximately 55%, depending on the products sold. Although these arrangements are beneficial, they inevitably result in an overall decrease in gross margin percentage. Therefore, the product mix is expected to continue to impact the overall gross margin percentage while increasing the gross profit and, given that expenses associated with this revenue do not increase significantly, the operating profit on a quarterly basis.

rd.text: On April 6, 2026, we entered into a ten-year agreement with the Biomedical Advanced Research and Development Authority (“BARDA”), part of the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, with a total potential value of up to $25.5 million. Under the agreement, we will maintain a supply of RECELL for deployment in mass casualty incidents and provide associated readiness and support services. The agreement provides approximately $4.0 million in access and maintenance fees over the ten-year term, with additional potential revenue tied to procurement options exercised by BARDA. Costs to fulfill the BARDA emergency preparedness performance obligation, which consist of billed costs to BARDA incurred in connection with emergency deployment services, are incremental and expected to be recovered.

sm.text: Sales and marketing expenses increased by 13%, or $1.5 million, to $13.6 million, compared to $12.1 million in the corresponding period in the prior year. Higher costs in the current year are due to increases in selling expenses of $1.5 million, primarily commission expense, and salaries and benefits of $1.0 million, primarily annual incentive compensation costs, offset by lower professional fees and consulting fees of $0.5 million, stock-based compensation of $0.3 million, and other selling expenses of $0.2 million.

ga.text: General and administrative expenses decreased by 13%, or $0.9 million, to $6.3 million, compared to $7.2 million in the same period in the prior year. Lower costs in the current year are due to decreases in professional fees of $0.8 million, stock-based compensation of $0.7 million, and other corporate expenses of $0.2 million, offset by an increase in salaries and benefits of $0.8 million. The decrease in professional fees is related to lower legal expenses. The decrease in stock-based compensation is due to reduced grant activity. The increase in salaries and benefits is due to higher annual incentive compensation costs.

intro.text: AVITA Medical is a leading therapeutic acute wound care company delivering transformative solutions designed to optimize wound healing, accelerate patient recovery, and improve clinical and economic outcomes across the continuum of acute wound management. Our technologies address critical healing needs arising from burns, traumatic injuries and surgical repairs, through a portfolio of proprietary and complementary products that support wound bed preparation, definitive closure, and recovery. Our current commercial portfolio includes RECELL ® (“RECELL”), and two complementary wound care products, PermeaDerm ® and Cohealyx ™ , which together support a comprehensive standard of care for acute wounds.

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Short-term investments
lines.why: Securities held for the cash they will return: financial.

lines.name: Long-term investments
lines.why: Securities held for their return: financial. A stake in another business that is part of operations is operating.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Inventory
lines.why: Goods held for sale: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current assets
lines.why: Other long-term operating items: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Deferred revenue
lines.why: Customers' payments ahead of delivery: operating.

lines.name: Other current liabilities
lines.why: Other operating items due within a year: operating.

lines.name: Current portion of long-term debt
lines.why: Borrowed money falling due within a year: financial.

lines.name: Long-term debt
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Deferred revenue, non-current
lines.why: Customers' payments for later years: operating.

lines.name: Other current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current assets minus the current lines above: current assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current assets (total assets − current assets) minus the non-current lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current liabilities minus the current lines above: current liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current liabilities (total liabilities − current liabilities) minus the non-current lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

accounts.note: The cash flow statement's cash can include restricted cash the balance sheet shows elsewhere: a small residual is that difference.

accounts.name: Investments
accounts.note: Securities bought and sold sit in 'other investing' with everything else the section does not name.

accounts.name: Property, plant and equipment
accounts.note: Depreciation and amortisation includes the amortisation of intangibles where the filing reports one line: the PP&E residual then carries the intangibles' share.

accounts.name: Goodwill and intangibles
accounts.note: Acquisitions add goodwill and intangibles at their allocated values, not at the cash paid; the residual is the difference and the amortisation.
